items.question: Can you draw a line through a heart shape so both sides look the same?

lessons.title: Line Symmetry: The Mirror Rule
lessons.objective: Learner can identify lines of symmetry in shapes.
teach: Imagine folding a paper shape in half.
If the two halves cover each other perfectly, the fold line is a 'Line of Symmetry'.
It is like placing a mirror on the line; one side is a reflection of the other.

worked_example.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
worked_example.method: 1. Fold vertically (Yes). 2. Fold horizontally (Yes). 3. Fold diagonally (Yes - both ways). 4. Total = 4 lines.

lessons.checkpoint: Does the letter 'A' have line symmetry?

lessons.title: Rotational Symmetry: The Spin Rule
lessons.objective: Learner can identify if a shape looks the same after being turned.
teach: Sometimes a shape doesn't look the same if folded, but it does if you SPIN it.
Take a ceiling fan. If you turn it slightly, it looks exactly like it did before.
The number of times it looks the same in one full turn is its 'Order of Rotation'.

worked_example.prompt: What is the order of rotational symmetry for an equilateral triangle?
worked_example.method: 1. Start at top. 2. Turn 120 degrees (looks same). 3. Turn 240 degrees (looks same). 4. Turn 360 degrees (back to start). 5. It looked same 3 times. Order = 3.

lessons.checkpoint: Does a rectangle have rotational symmetry?

lessons.title: Both Line and Rotation
lessons.objective: Learner can identify shapes that have both types of symmetry.
teach: A circle is the king of symmetry. It has infinite lines of symmetry and infinite rotational symmetry.
Regular polygons (shapes with equal sides) usually have the same number of lines as their order of rotation.

worked_example.prompt: A regular hexagon has how many lines of symmetry and what order of rotation?
worked_example.method: 1. A hexagon has 6 equal sides. 2. It has 6 lines of symmetry. 3. It has rotational symmetry of order 6.

lessons.checkpoint: True or False: A square has order 4 rotational symmetry.

items.question: Which of these letters has vertical line symmetry?
items.explanation: If you draw a vertical line down the middle of 'M', both sides are identical.

items.question: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
items.explanation: Any line passing through the center of a circle is a line of symmetry.

items.question: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a square?
items.explanation: A square looks the same every 90-degree turn, which happens 4 times in a full circle.

items.question: A rectangle has rotational symmetry of order:
items.explanation: A rectangle looks the same after a 180-degree turn and a 360-degree turn.

items.question: Which figure has only 1 line of symmetry but NO rotational symmetry (order 1)?
items.explanation: An isosceles triangle has one line of symmetry (down the middle) but only looks the same after a full 360-degree turn.

items.question: Which of these shapes has exactly 3 lines of symmetry?
items.explanation: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry, one through each vertex.

items.question: If a shape has rotational symmetry of order 4, what is the angle of rotation?
Which of these has no line of symmetry?
items.explanation: Letter Z has rotational symmetry but no line of symmetry.

items.question: Which letter has both line and rotational symmetry?
items.explanation: Wait, 'H' has both (horizontal/vertical lines and order 2 rotation). 'A' only has line. 'T' only has line. 'E' only has line. Correct answer is 'H'.

items.question: A regular pentagon has how many lines of symmetry?
items.explanation: A regular polygon with 'n' sides has 'n' lines of symmetry.

misconception_remediation.diagnostic: Check if learner thinks 'Z' has line symmetry.
repair: Physically fold a paper 'Z' to show the parts don't match.
Spin the 'Z' to show it looks the same upside down (rotational).
misconception_remediation.exit_criterion: Learner correctly identifies 'S' and 'Z' as having rotational but no line symmetry.

misconception_remediation.trigger: Thinking every turn is a symmetry
misconception_remediation.diagnostic: Check if learner thinks a scalene triangle has rotational symmetry.
repair: Explain that 'Order 1' means it only looks the same after a full 360 degree turn, which means it has NO special rotational symmetry.
Use a 'starting mark' to track the turn.
misconception_remediation.exit_criterion: Learner identifies order of rotation for irregular shapes as 1.

misconception_remediation.diagnostic: Check if learner thinks a rectangle has diagonal lines of symmetry.
repair: Fold a rectangular paper diagonally to show the corners do not meet.
Contrast this with a square where corners DO meet.
misconception_remediation.exit_criterion: Learner correctly states a rectangle has only 2 lines of symmetry.
